To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) in dynamic MIMO–OFDMA systems, it is possible to achieve the same energy efficiency as in the static regime, even when users cannot predict how the system will change over time, and (ii) this result can be achieved even when channel state information is noisy and imperfect.

(1) we propose a simple distributed online algorithm to maximize energy efficiency in dynamic MIMO-OFDMA systems; (2) the algorithm is provably optimal, i.e., achieves no-regret performance in hindsight; (3) the algorithm is robust to imperfect channel knowledge; (4) the algorithm is scalable, i.e., can be applied to massive MIMO systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of energy-efficient wireless networks that are capable of adapting to dynamic and uncertain operating conditions.

the design of energy-efficient policies for dynamic MIMO-OFDMA systems, and provides an answer to the question: How can users learn to be green in the presence of time-varying channel conditions and limited CSI?
developing a new generation of algorithms for wireless communication that are able to adapt to dynamic environments, and that can be implemented in a decentralized manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithm achieves the same performance as the optimal one, even in the worst-case scenario, and that the performance gap between the two is negligible.
the proposed algorithm is a simple, yet powerful, online policy that allows users to maximize EE, even when the system is dynamic and noisy.
the proposed policy is robust and performs well even under rapidly changing conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an online optimization algorithm to maximize the energy efficiency in a MIMO-OFDMA system, where the channel state varies with time.
the proposed online algorithm is robust and achieves no-regret performance, i.e. it is able to match the best offline policy in hindsight.
we provide a simple, robust, and distributed algorithm for energy efficiency maximization in dynamic MIMO-OFDMA networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the online optimization framework can serve as a powerful tool to tackle the challenges of dynamic wireless networks, while also accounting for the practical constraints of massive MIMO.

, even in the presence of imperfect CSI and dynamic network conditions, it is still possible to design distributed algorithms with provably good performance guarantees, which can be implemented with low computational overhead.
, in dynamic systems, users can learn to be green by adjusting their transmit powers on the fly, without the need for any a priori CSI or knowledge about the system's dynamics.
